title: TypeScript
description: Generics, utility types, discriminated unions, narrowing, module resolution. Heavy on Turing MCQ, medium on FDE loop.

questions.prompt: Which is NOT a TypeScript primitive type keyword?
questions.explanation: TS uses `number` for all numeric values. `float` doesn't exist.

questions.prompt: What is the key difference between `any` and `unknown`?

options.text: `any` disables type checking; `unknown` requires narrowing before use

questions.explanation: `unknown` is the type-safe counterpart to `any`. You must narrow (typeof, instanceof) before using it.

questions.prompt: Which type is inferred?
questions.explanation: T is inferred as `number`, so return type becomes `number | undefined`.

questions.prompt: `Partial<T>` produces:

options.text: A type with all properties of T made optional
A type with all properties readonly

questions.explanation: `Partial<T>` maps each key to optional. `Readonly<T>` freezes, `Pick<T,K>` selects, `Omit<T,K>` removes.

questions.prompt: Given `type User = { id: string; name: string; email: string }`, which produce `{ name: string; email: string }`? (select all)
questions.explanation: Pick selects keys; Omit removes keys. Exclude operates on unions of types, not object keys.

questions.prompt: Does this compile?

options.text: No — toFixed doesn't exist on `string | number`

questions.explanation: TypeScript narrows `x` to `number` after the `typeof === 'string'` branch returns.

questions.prompt: What lets TS narrow `s`?

options.text: It doesn't narrow — needs a cast

questions.explanation: Discriminated (tagged) unions rely on a shared literal-type property; TS narrows on that check.

questions.prompt: `type X = string extends string | number ? 'a' : 'b'` is:
questions.explanation: `string` is assignable to `string | number`, so the check succeeds → 'a'.

questions.prompt: Given `type NonNull<T> = T extends null | undefined ? never : T`, what is `NonNull<string | null | number>`?
questions.explanation: Conditional types distribute over unions. Each member is tested; null → never → dropped from union.

questions.prompt: Which is TRUE about `interface` vs `type`?
questions.explanation: Declaration merging is interface-only. Both compile to nothing at runtime. Both can be extended (interface extends, type via intersection).

questions.prompt: Does this compile?

options.text: No, T must be the same for both args

questions.explanation: Both a and b are `T`, so TS tries to find one T that fits both string and number[]. Constraint doesn't help — error unless you use two generics.

questions.prompt: What does `type ReadOnly<T> = { readonly [K in keyof T]: T[K] }` do?

options.text: Marks every property of T as readonly

questions.explanation: Mapped type iterates keys of T, keeps original value types, adds `readonly`. This is the built-in `Readonly<T>`.

questions.prompt: What is the inferred type of `const x = { role: 'admin' } as const`?
questions.explanation: `as const` narrows to literal types AND makes properties readonly.

questions.prompt: Which is TRUE about numeric enums?

options.text: They create a reverse-map object at runtime

questions.explanation: Numeric enums emit runtime code with two-way mapping. `const enum` inlines and disappears. String enums also emit but no reverse map.

questions.prompt: What is `type K = keyof { a: 1; b: 2; c: 3 }`?
questions.explanation: `keyof` produces a union of the object type's keys as string literal types.

questions.prompt: `ReturnType<T>` where `T = () => Promise<string>` is:
questions.explanation: ReturnType extracts the return of the function type as-is. To unwrap the Promise use `Awaited<ReturnType<T>>`.

questions.prompt: Given `type Elem<T> = T extends (infer U)[] ? U : never`, what is `Elem<string[]>`?
questions.explanation: `infer` captures the array element type inside a conditional. Works like unification.

questions.prompt: Which are valid TS type guards? (select all)

options.text: function isCat(x: any): x is Cat { return x.meow !== undefined }

questions.explanation: All narrow. User-defined type predicates use `x is T` return type.

questions.prompt: When is `never` useful?

options.text: For exhaustiveness checks in switch statements

questions.explanation: Assigning to `never` in a `default:` branch causes a compile error if the union isn't exhausted.

questions.prompt: What is `type E = `${"user" | "admin"}_${"read" | "write"}``?
questions.explanation: Template literal types distribute across union parts.

questions.prompt: With `strictNullChecks` ON, this fails to compile — why?
questions.explanation: With strict null checks, `null` and `undefined` are only assignable to their own types (or explicit unions like `string | null`).

questions.prompt: You import a JS lib with no types. What's the minimal fix?
questions.explanation: A minimal ambient module declaration silences the compile error. Ideal: install @types/mylib if it exists.

questions.prompt: Write a generic `pluck` function: given `T[]` and a key `K extends keyof T`, return `T[K][]`.
Write a `DeepPartial<T>` type that recursively makes every property optional.
Given `Cat extends Animal`, is `Cat[]` assignable to `Animal[]` in TS?
questions.explanation: TS treats arrays covariantly (unsound but pragmatic). Function parameter positions are bivariant unless `strictFunctionTypes` is on (then contravariant).
